title: On Destroying the bridge in one night
subtitle: 战争和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：destroy　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 destroy 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the grandmother ① destroyed the bridge in one night before dawn, and every child in the courtyard said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the grandmother ② destroys the bridge in one night in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ destroy the bridge in one night at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ destroyed the bridge in one night before — a line in the diary for February 1946 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Destroying the bridge in one night before dawn, the grandmother said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lamp at the far window, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ destroy every copy of the letter in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Destroy every copy of the letter at once and never mention it again.

By 1959 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the diary, and a new child from the next courtyard ⑧ destroys every copy of the letter before dawn every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the window, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ destroyed the bridge in one night again when nobody else would.

⑩ To destroy the bridge in one night, my mother said in 1964, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the courtyard remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the courtyard forgets, somebody destroys the bridge in one night in public again and somebody must destroy the bridge in one night before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 摧毁（一般过去式 destroyed the bridge in one night：1952 年祖母头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 摧毁（一般现在 destroys the bridge in one night：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 摧毁（不定式 to destroy the bridge in one night：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 摧毁（过去完成时 had destroyed the bridge in one night：1946 年二月的日记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 摧毁（动名词 destroying the bridge in one night 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 毁掉（destroy every copy of the letter：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去毁掉把那封信的每一份都销毁）
G. v. 毁掉（destroy every copy of the letter：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 摧毁（后段两处：新来的孩子照例 destroys every copy of the letter，而母亲又一次 destroyed the bridge in one night）

answers.why: destroy 意为“摧毁”，1952 年祖母天没亮就摧毁一夜之间毁掉那座桥，那是院子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 destroyed。
destroy 意为“摧毁”，自那以后祖母当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 destroys。
destroy 意为“摧毁”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯摧毁一夜之间毁掉那座桥”，此处为不定式 to destroy the bridge in one night。
destroy 意为“摧毁”，日记里 二月 那行字说明早在 1959 年之前就有人摧毁过，故用过去完成时 had destroyed。
destroy 意为“摧毁”，祖母说“摧毁一夜之间毁掉那座桥这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 destroying the bridge in one night 作主语。
destroy 意为“毁掉”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去毁掉把那封信的每一份都销毁”，should ever 之后用原形 destroy every copy of the letter。
destroy 意为“毁掉”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻毁掉把那封信的每一份都销毁（destroy every copy of the letter at once），以后再也不要提起。
destroy 意为“摧毁”，新来的孩子每个年头都照例毁掉把那封信的每一份都销毁，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 destroys。
destroy 意为“摧毁”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就摧毁一夜之间毁掉那座桥，用一般过去式 destroyed 叙述。
destroy 意为“摧毁”，结尾那句是母亲 1964 年的话：要摧毁一夜之间毁掉那座桥，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和院子记住的那一件。

多年以后，祖母仍当着众人面做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（destroys the bridge in one night）

早在 1946 年就有人摧毁一夜之间毁掉那座桥，二月那天日记上的一行字就是证据。（had destroyed the bridge in one night）
祖母说过，天没亮就摧毁一夜之间毁掉那座桥这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（destroying the bridge in one night 作主语）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 destroy 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1952 the grandmother destroyed the bridge in one night before dawn, and nobody in the courtyard forgot it.
Even now the grandmother destroys the bridge in one night in public whenever the courtyard asks.
Destroying the bridge in one night before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever destroy every copy of the letter in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new child from the next courtyard destroys every copy of the letter before dawn every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother destroyed the bridge in one night again, and the courtyard remembered that half.
